9602907756.description: Physicist detective Manabu Yukawa travels to a struggling seaside resort town for a mining conference, only to be pulled into a murder investigation when a guest is found dead at the base of the cliffs. Kirkus called it ingenious in working one twist after another in a case that seems absolutely twist proof, and The Times dubbed Higashino the Japanese Stieg Larsson. The third book in the internationally bestselling Detective Galileo series, later adapted into a hit Japanese film. 3.96 stars on Goodreads. #japanesecrimefiction #detectivegalileo #mysterythriller

9602894095.description: Four women left their regular lives behind for fifty six days to ride motorbikes 17,000 kilometres across six countries, from Hyderabad through India's northeast, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos and Vietnam along the Mekong River to Cambodia. Piya Bahadur recounts a once in a lifetime journey through terrain rarely seen by Indian travellers, and her own transformation from an inhibited working mother into a confident adventurer. Praised by Incredible India's Director General of Tourism as an exhilarating read. #motorcycletravel #womenwhotravel #adventurememoir

9602879226.description: A forbidden love story between a Sunni boy and Shia girl unfolds against the backdrop of 1990s Kashmir, as war and political violence close in on their world. Shortlisted for the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature and longlisted for the Folio Prize, the Financial Times called it a work that will undoubtedly endure. From the author of the international bestseller The Collaborator, praised by Arundhati Roy as fiction that makes you listen #kashmirliterature #southasianfiction #warfiction

9602870728.description: The timeless Mahabharata retold entirely from the perspective of Panchaali, wife of the five Pandava brothers, tracing her fiery birth, her complicated bond with Krishna, and her forbidden attraction to her husbands' most dangerous enemy. The Los Angeles Times called it a bright gem as the Hope Diamond, and the Houston Chronicle called it radiant and charming. A deeply human, half history, half myth story of a woman born into a man's world. 4.20 stars on Goodreads. #mahabharata #mythicalfiction #internationalbestseller

9602838102.description: A quietly devastating novel about a humble couple exiled by their own families for marrying without consent, whose fragile peace is shattered when a debt forces a reckoning with the past. Natsume Soseki called this his favorite among all his own novels, and Haruki Murakami has cited it as the book he identifies with most strongly. The New Statesman called it a masterpiece of taste and clarity. This NYRB edition offers a new, more accurate translation than earlier versions. 4.07 stars on Goodreads. #japaneseliterature #natsumesoseki #nyrbclassics

9602824787.description: Written when Neruda was only nineteen, this collection of sensual, aching love poetry launched him onto the world stage and remains one of the most celebrated poetry collections ever published. Neruda went on to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, and this book is still considered one of the most romantic and intensely personal works of poetry ever written. This Penguin Classics Deluxe Edition includes illustrations by Pablo Picasso. 4.19 stars on Goodreads. #poetry #pabloneruda #lovepoems

9602788500.description: The most influential book ever written on the origins of nationalism, examining what drives people to live, die, and kill for their nation. Essential reading for anyone interested in political theory, history, or global politics. 4.11 stars on Goodreads. #politicaltheory #nationalism #academicbooks

9602779694.description: A groundbreaking, meticulously researched account of the 21 month suspension of Indian democracy under Indira Gandhi, called the best and most wide ranging account of the Emergency ever written. Winner of the Karwaan Prize. 3.75 stars on Goodreads. #indianhistory #politics #nonfiction

9602746361.description: An energetic, counterintuitive exploration of why and how underdogs succeed, from small class sizes to civil rights battles to disadvantages that turn into hidden strengths.
